title: Separate display and reading roles
rule: Treat display type and body/UI type as separate jobs unless one family demonstrably handles both.
rationale: Expressive headings and long-form readability have different constraints.

title: Contrast pairings by role
rule: When pairing fonts, create meaningful contrast in voice, proportions or texture instead of selecting two nearly identical sans serifs.
rationale: A strong role contrast makes the hierarchy legible and avoids accidental-looking pairings.

title: Limit active families
rule: Default to one or two families; add a third only when it represents a distinct content role.
rationale: Too many families weaken visual coherence and increase loading cost.

title: Use variable fonts deliberately
rule: Prefer variable fonts when a project genuinely uses multiple weights/widths/axes.
rationale: They can reduce the cost of loading many separate font files and allow finer art direction.

title: Do not use display fonts for dense copy
rule: Keep highly stylized faces away from long paragraphs, dense tables and controls.
rationale: Distinctive letterforms can reduce reading speed and UI clarity.

title: Define a type scale
rule: Create named tokens for display, h1-h6, body, small, label and caption instead of ad-hoc sizes.
rationale: A type scale gives hierarchy consistency across pages and responsive states.

title: Fluid type needs accessible bounds
rule: Use clamp/min/max strategies that preserve zoom/user font preferences rather than pure viewport units.
rationale: Fluid type should respond to viewport without overriding user control.

title: Control measure
rule: Set comfortable line lengths for body copy rather than letting paragraphs span arbitrary wide containers.
rationale: Line length is a composition variable, not an afterthought.

title: Tune line-height by role
rule: Display headings can be tight; paragraph text and UI labels need different line-height systems.
rationale: One global line-height produces weak rhythm.

title: Tune tracking by size
rule: Large display type often tolerates tighter tracking; all-caps labels usually need more tracking.
rationale: Optical spacing changes with size and casing.

title: Avoid fake font weights
rule: Do not rely on browser-synthesized bold/italic when real faces/axes exist.
rationale: Synthetic styles can distort intended design.

title: Use optical size where available
rule: If a variable font has opsz, test it for text and display roles rather than freezing one setting.
rationale: Optical-size axes can improve shapes for different point sizes.

title: Respect script/language coverage
rule: Verify required glyphs, Turkish characters and punctuation before choosing a display font.
rationale: Missing glyphs or fallback mixing destroys visual consistency.

title: Fallback metrics matter
rule: Define compatible fallbacks and consider size-adjust/metric overrides for large web fonts.
rationale: Reducing metric mismatch can reduce layout shift.

title: Preload only critical fonts
rule: Preload only font files needed above the fold; avoid preloading every weight.
rationale: Over-preloading competes with more important resources.

title: Create font-loading states
rule: Ensure layout remains usable before custom fonts load.
rationale: The experience should not depend on a blank-font phase.

title: Numbers are a distinct typographic role
rule: Check tabular/proportional numerals for dashboards, prices and counters.
rationale: Numeric content can require alignment behavior different from prose.

title: Use hierarchy before decoration
rule: Use size, weight, spacing and contrast before adding gradients, outlines or glow to text.
rationale: Decoration cannot repair weak hierarchy.

title: Avoid center-aligning long copy
rule: Reserve centered alignment for short statements or intentional compositions.
rationale: Long centered text is harder to scan and often signals generic landing-page layout.

title: Create editorial contrast
rule: Combine scale changes, width changes, italics, serif/sans contrast or density shifts intentionally.
rationale: Editorial rhythm can make pages distinctive without extra cards/effects.

title: Use text width as composition
rule: A heading can be narrow, wide, stacked or offset; do not force every headline into the same max-width.
rationale: Text block shape is part of visual composition.

title: Define casing rules
rule: Specify where uppercase, title case and sentence case belong.
rationale: Random casing makes interfaces feel assembled rather than art-directed.

title: Define punctuation style
rule: Decide how dashes, quotes, slashes and numbered labels appear in art-directed layouts.
rationale: Micro-typography adds consistency.

title: Use display fonts sparingly
rule: A distinctive typeface is more memorable when concentrated in high-value moments.
rationale: Overuse turns character into noise.

title: Body contrast must pass accessibility
rule: Keep paragraph and control text at sufficient contrast against its background.
rationale: Readability is a non-negotiable quality gate.

title: Build responsive line breaks
rule:
Do not hardcode desktop
line breaks that become awkward on mobile; use responsive variants or natural wrapping.
rationale: Editorial line breaks are viewport-specific.

title: Keep labels compact
rule: Navigation, chips and controls should use concise language and stable metrics.
rationale: UI typography should optimize recognition, not display drama.

title: Animate text by semantic unit
rule: Choose character, word, line or block animation based on reading intent.
rationale: Animating every character independently can reduce comprehension.

title: Split-text must be reversible
rule: Any split-text implementation should restore on resize/unmount and preserve accessibility.
rationale: Responsive text reflow can invalidate line wrappers.

title: Do not scramble critical copy
rule: Scramble/glitch effects belong to short decorative moments, not essential instructions.
rationale: Legibility must win over spectacle.

title: Use hierarchy tokens in 3D scenes
rule: DOM annotations, 3D labels and normal page text should share a coherent type system.
rationale: 3D overlays should not look like a separate product.

title: Support reduced motion in kinetic type
rule: Provide static or simpler reveals when reduced motion is requested.
rationale: Text remains content even when animation is removed.

title: Avoid default Inter-everywhere behavior
rule: System/Inter-like sans can be valid, but require a reason and supporting art direction.
rationale: The problem is defaulting, not the font itself.

title: Use content to choose font mood
rule: Map font characteristics to brand voice: technical, editorial, playful, institutional, luxurious, raw, etc.
rationale: Type choice should be project-specific.

title: Pair width with layout density
rule: Condensed display faces can support narrow columns; wide faces need room.
rationale: Typeface proportions influence grid decisions.

title: Test real content extremes
rule: Test long names, Turkish diacritics, 4-digit numbers, error messages and multiline buttons.
rationale: Type systems should survive production content.

title: Do not rely on font alone for hierarchy
rule: Combine spacing, grouping and color with typography.
rationale: Hierarchy is multimodal.

title: Use italic as a role, not decoration
rule: Define whether italic means emphasis, voice, quote or editorial contrast.
rationale: Consistent semantics strengthen design.

title: Create font licenses/availability metadata
rule: Every font recipe should record license/source/hosting constraints.
rationale: A library cannot recommend fonts that cannot legally or practically ship.

title: Track performance cost
rule: Font catalog entries should include file count, variable/static mode and estimated loading impact.
rationale: Premium typography should not quietly destroy performance.

title: Catalog pairing archetypes
rule: Store pairings as archetypes (neutral+expressive, grotesk+serif, mono+humanist, etc.), not only font names.
rationale: Archetypes transfer to new projects even when fonts change.

title: Near-black text can create softer dark themes
rule: Tinted near-black can reduce the harshness of pure black when the art direction calls for it.
rationale: Shinobi indexed posts repeatedly showcase near-black alternatives; treat this as an option, not a universal rule.

title: Do not encode Shinobi examples as laws
rule: Font lists from a creator should become references, not mandatory defaults.
rationale: A library should preserve principles while preventing stylistic cloning.

title: Typography needs visual QA
rule: Screenshot the same type system at mobile, tablet and wide desktop.
rationale: Metrics that look good in code may fail visually.

title: Store text-motion compatibility
rule: Each text effect should declare which type sizes and content lengths it supports.
rationale: Effects that work on a one-line hero may break a paragraph.

title: Use semantic color roles
rule: Define background, surface, text, muted, accent, success, warning, danger and focus roles rather than scattering hex values.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Pure black is optional, not mandatory
rule: Test tinted near-black values for dark interfaces when softer contrast or brand tone is desired.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Do not ban pure black globally
rule: Pure black can be correct for a specific identity, OLED-focused art direction or sharp editorial contrast.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Build palettes from relationships
rule: Store hue, lightness and contrast relationships instead of only fixed swatches.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: One accent can be enough
rule: Use a single strong accent when the composition already has rich imagery or 3D.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Separate brand accent from status colors
rule: Do not reuse the brand color for destructive/success states if meaning becomes ambiguous.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Text contrast is a gate
rule: Normal text should meet WCAG minimum contrast against its actual background.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Large text still needs contrast
rule: Large display text has a lower minimum ratio than body text but should still be validated.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Do not communicate state by color alone
rule: Pair color with icon, label, shape or text where state matters.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Dark mode needs luminance layers
rule: Create multiple dark surface levels rather than black background + glowing cards.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Light mode needs surface hierarchy
rule: Use subtle tonal differences and borders where needed; not every section needs a grey card.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Avoid default AI purple-blue
rule: Purple/blue gradients require a brand or content reason, not an AI/tech stereotype.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Gradient has a job
rule: Use gradients for depth, material, state, atmosphere or brand—not filler.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Keep gradient count low
rule: Multiple unrelated gradients quickly destroy palette coherence.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Use color temperature intentionally
rule: Warm/cool shifts can separate foreground/background or emotional states.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Use saturation as hierarchy
rule: Not every object should be fully saturated; reserve saturation for focus.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Image palette should influence UI
rule: When a hero image/3D model dominates, derive surrounding neutrals/accents from it where appropriate.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: 3D lighting and DOM palette must agree
rule: WebGL scene and HTML should appear in the same color world.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Emissive colors need headroom
rule: Do not set every bright material to maximum intensity; selective emission makes bloom meaningful.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Color recipes need contrast metadata
rule: Palette catalog records should store text-on-bg pass/fail pairs.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Catalog dark alternatives
rule: Store several near-black families: neutral, warm, cool, green-tinted, red-tinted.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Catalog off-whites
rule: Store warm/cool/neutral off-white families for softer editorial themes.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Use black/white extremes intentionally
rule: Extremes can create brutalist/editorial impact when hierarchy is clear.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Avoid low-contrast grey-on-grey UI
rule: Muted does not mean unreadable.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Focus indicators are part of palette
rule: Define focus colors and contrast as first-class tokens.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Hover color should preserve meaning
rule: Hover should not make text or controls fail contrast.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Selected state needs more than tiny hue shift
rule: Use border, fill, scale, icon or type changes if hue difference is too subtle.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Color transitions should be synchronized
rule: When scene background changes, text/surface colors should transition as a coordinated state.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Use color chaptering selectively
rule: Long narratives can assign distinct controlled palettes to chapters.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Do not auto-generate rainbow palettes
rule: Large color sets should have semantic or narrative logic.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Record palette mood as metadata
rule: Catalog palettes with descriptors such as industrial, editorial, playful, luxury, organic.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Record display context
rule: A palette proven on dark hero art may fail in dense dashboard tables.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Shinobi palette examples are references
rule: Indexed combinations like Deep Sea/Sea Foam and high-contrast pairings should inspire palette archetypes, not be mandatory.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Tinted black library should include source examples
rule: Preserve indexed near-black examples as reference swatches with source labels.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Test with screenshots and browser rendering
rule: Color changes in 3D post-processing and display profiles can alter perceived results.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Never invent exact colors from inaccessible reels
rule: Mark unviewed reel palettes NEEDS_CAPTURE until visual evidence is supplied.
rationale: Color should support hierarchy, meaning, accessibility and art direction.

title: Content determines section count
rule: Do not generate sections just to fill a landing-page template.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Avoid three-card default
rule: Feature count and structure should follow content, not a repeated three-column pattern.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Use cards only for true containers
rule: Whitespace, rules and alignment can group content without card chrome.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Build a spacing scale
rule: Use named spacing tokens rather than arbitrary per-section values.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Rhythm can vary
rule: Dense and open sections can alternate intentionally; identical py values everywhere look templated.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Asymmetry is a tool
rule: Offset columns, uneven widths and controlled imbalance can create identity without harming usability.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Grid should support content
rule: Choose column count/gutters from content density and media, not from framework defaults.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Editorial pages need text-image relationships
rule: Use overlap, offsets, captions and scale relationships instead of card grids when appropriate.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Hero does not have to be centered
rule: Explore split, object-led, editorial, edge-aligned, immersive or navigational heroes.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Navigation geometry belongs to brand
rule: Floating pill nav is one option, not the default.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Use container width deliberately
rule: Different content roles may use different max widths within one system.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Full-bleed media needs anchors
rule: When media spans viewport, maintain alignment anchors to connect it to text.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Whitespace is an active element
rule: Space should create hierarchy and pacing, not merely fill leftovers.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Avoid bento without hierarchy
rule: Mixed card sizes should reflect information importance or interaction differences.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Preserve scan paths
rule: Experimental composition still needs a clear first, second and action target.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Sticky sections need evolution
rule: Pinned sections should change enough to justify the scroll cost.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Horizontal scroll needs a reason
rule: Use it for sequences, galleries or spatial journeys—not novelty.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Mobile can reorder narrative
rule: Do not force desktop layer order onto narrow screens.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Touch targets need room
rule: Visual density cannot reduce interactive target usability.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: 3D canvas and DOM share grid
rule: Define anchors that allow 3D objects to align with text columns and UI.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Use negative space around focal 3D object
rule: Do not cover a model with UI simply because the canvas is large.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: World labels need collision strategy
rule: Projected DOM labels should hide, offset or cluster when they overlap.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Z-depth should correspond to motion
rule: Foreground/midground/background layers need different parallax amplitudes.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Long stories need chapters
rule: Use section states and progress markers when a narrative spans many viewport heights.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Do not make every section full-screen
rule: Full-screen moments are strongest when contrasted with normal-flow content.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Design loading layout too
rule: Reserve space and states for 3D/video/font loading to prevent layout chaos.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Define safe areas for UI over 3D
rule: Camera/model motion should respect persistent nav, CTA and text zones.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Build responsive breakpoint profiles
rule: Desktop/tablet/mobile can have different camera and composition states.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Grid tokens should include gutter and margin
rule: Column count alone is not a grid system.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Use alignment repetition selectively
rule: Repeated anchors create coherence; breaking them creates emphasis.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Design for long localization
rule: Buttons/navigation/labels must survive text expansion.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Overlaps need escape rules
rule: Set responsive conditions that remove risky overlaps on small screens.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Hero object can define the grid
rule: A dominant model/product can create natural text zones around its silhouette.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Background decoration cannot compete
rule: Decorative layers should support focal hierarchy.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Create section archetypes, not templates
rule: Store composition recipes such as editorial split, object focus, annotated model, timeline, immersive chapter.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Recipe metadata needs density
rule: Mark layouts compact/normal/spacious so agents combine compatible modules.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Recipe metadata needs media role
rule: Mark whether photo/video/3D/text is primary so selection is intentional.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Avoid copy-paste component geometry
rule: A library can share mechanics while allowing each project to vary layout.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Screenshot QA across widths
rule: Visual QA is mandatory for composition-heavy work.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Reference analysis should record proportions
rule: Capture relative column widths, alignment, media scale and whitespace—not just colors.
rationale: Layout quality comes from hierarchy, rhythm, content structure and responsive art direction.

title: Create one motion language
rule: Define shared easing/duration/weight principles for UI, text, camera and objects.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Motion needs purpose
rule: Animation should communicate state, hierarchy, causality, spatial change or narrative progression.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Avoid universal fade-up
rule: Do not attach opacity+translateY to every element.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Use stillness
rule: Not everything should move continuously; rest makes motion meaningful.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Different masses move differently
rule: Large 3D objects, UI labels and camera should not share identical timing.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Use frame-rate-independent damping
rule: Interactive follow motion should use delta-aware damping/springs.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Centralize frame loops
rule: Avoid unmanaged requestAnimationFrame loops per module.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Pause inactive work
rule: Use visibility/offscreen signals to reduce animation work.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Prefer transforms for DOM motion
rule: Use transform/opacity for common motion where possible.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Scroll is a normalized signal
rule: Expose 0..1 progress that can drive DOM, WebGL and shaders.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Velocity is secondary
rule: Scroll velocity can add inertia but should not overpower content.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Pinned scenes need chapters
rule: Map ranges of scroll to explicit states rather than dozens of unrelated tweens.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Timelines should be inspectable
rule: Use named timelines and labels for complex sequences.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Transitions should preserve context
rule: Persistent objects/camera continuity can make section changes feel spatial.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Route transitions should be brief
rule: Do not hide navigation speed behind long cinematic transitions.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Hover must not be required
rule: Touch and keyboard users need equivalent interaction paths.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Magnetic motion must be small
rule: Never make the user chase a button.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Cursor effects are optional
rule: Disable or simplify custom cursor logic on touch/coarse pointers.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Text reveal unit must match content
rule: Animate by line/word/character based on reading goal.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Scramble effects are decorative
rule: Do not scramble essential information or forms.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Clip/mask reveals need fallback
rule: Content must remain visible without animation.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Reduced motion is centralized
rule: All modules should subscribe to one motion-preference signal.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Camera follows slower than pointer
rule: Subtle lag makes camera response weighted; direct 1:1 mapping often feels cheap.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Avoid motion on every pointer move
rule: Only selected scene elements should react.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Scroll-scrub video should have poster fallback
rule: Heavy video timelines need resilience.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Do not smooth-scroll by default
rule: Native scroll can be best; opt into smooth scrolling when it benefits the experience.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: One gesture should have one dominant response
rule: Avoid cursor simultaneously rotating model, moving camera, warping shader and moving typography at full strength.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Use easing families
rule: Create UI, object and camera easing tokens instead of random cubic-bezier values.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Keep durations contextual
rule: Micro feedback fast; scene changes slower; loading intro short.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Stagger by hierarchy
rule: Stagger order should reflect reading/visual order.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Do not stagger huge lists
rule: Large repeated items need batching/virtualization, not theatrical delay.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Animate state, not CSS soup
rule: Prefer named states/timelines over scattered property mutations.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Measure animation performance
rule: Track frame time and dropped frames on representative devices.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Post-processing can animate too
rule: Bloom/DOF/color grade may transition between scene states, but subtly.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Lighting transitions can replace UI effects
rule: A light shift can reveal a feature more elegantly than adding overlays.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Use motion to explain 3D construction
rule: Assembly/exploded views should reveal relationships, not random movement.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: 3D motion should preserve orientation cues
rule: Do not spin products so aggressively that users lose spatial understanding.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Camera cuts are rare on web
rule: Prefer interpolated moves unless a deliberate hard cut serves the concept.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Pointer inertia should decay
rule: Velocity-driven effects need a clear return to rest.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Animation cleanup is mandatory
rule: Kill timelines/listeners/observers on unmount or route change.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Resize should refresh timelines
rule: Scroll ranges and text splits may change after resize/fonts load.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Loading exit belongs to timeline
rule: Preloader, first scene and first headline should transition as one sequence.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Do not fake loading progress
rule: Bind loaders to actual asset progress where possible.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Motion recipes need performance cost
rule: Catalog low/medium/high motion/effect cost.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Motion recipes need compatibility
rule: Declare whether an effect works with smooth-scroll, R3F, mobile, reduced-motion.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Motion recipes need parameters
rule: Expose amplitude, damping, duration, easing, trigger and range.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Reference analysis should capture timing relationships
rule: Note which event triggers what and relative pace, not imagined exact milliseconds.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Do not infer frame-perfect easing from inaccessible video
rule: Mark it NEEDS_CAPTURE.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Avoid perpetual decorative loops
rule: Continuous idle loops need strong brand/ambient purpose.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Use animation as transition between layouts
rule: FLIP-like transformations can maintain object continuity when geometry changes.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: 3D hover highlight should coordinate with DOM
rule: Hovered model part and its label/card should share state.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: Interaction feedback should begin quickly
rule: Even cinematic sites need prompt acknowledgment of input.
rationale: Motion should be coherent, performant, accessible and tied to interaction or story.

title: 3D must have a role
rule: Classify 3D as product, navigation, narrative, atmosphere, explanation or interaction before building.

title: Do not bolt model onto template

title: Teach the relationship, not only the swatches
rule: When proposing a palette, explain dominance, harmony, role assignment, area and contrast.
rationale: A reusable design intelligence library should make future agents understand why a combination works.

title: Start from role architecture
rule: Choose background/surface/text/accent/status roles before decorative colors.
rationale: Role-first palettes transfer better across components and themes.

title: Classify visual driver first
rule: Decide whether typography, imagery, 3D, data or illustration is the primary visual driver before choosing palette complexity.
rationale: Rich visual drivers often need simpler UI color systems.

title: Use monochromatic systems for restraint
rule: Prefer monochromatic families when imagery, typography or 3D already provides enough visual complexity.
rationale: A single hue family can preserve coherence without visual boredom when lightness and material vary.

title: Use analogous systems for atmosphere
rule: Use neighboring hue families when the design needs a cohesive atmospheric transition.
rationale: Analogous hues create softer separation than complementary pairs.

title: Use complementary color as a focal tool
rule: Use the opposite hue family primarily to create focal contrast, not as an equal-area second background.
rationale: Equal strong complements can create visual conflict.

title: Split complements need hierarchy
rule: Promote only one split-complement color to primary accent; keep the other supportive.
rationale: Three strong accent families quickly destroy hierarchy.

title: Triads need unequal weight
rule: In triadic systems, make one hue dominant, one secondary and one sparse.
rationale: Equal-area triads often look childish or noisy in UI.

title: Area is part of palette design
rule: Evaluate colors in approximate screen area, not only as equal swatches.
rationale: A small strong accent can work even if the same hue overwhelms at large area.

title: Accent scarcity increases value
rule: Keep the strongest chroma scarce unless brand art direction explicitly requires a large color field.
rationale: Scarcity makes action and signature details easier to notice.

title: Saturation can encode hierarchy
rule: Reduce chroma for support colors before reaching for opacity everywhere.
rationale: Chroma differences preserve cleaner, more predictable states.

title: Lightness creates structure
rule: Use lightness steps to separate surfaces and content levels.
rationale: A strong luminance structure reduces dependence on borders, shadows and glow.

title: Temperature can separate depth
rule: Use warm/cool relationships to distinguish foreground, background or narrative states when justified.
rationale: Temperature creates depth without requiring high saturation.

title: Tint neutrals subtly
rule: Warm, cool or colored neutrals should support atmosphere without announcing themselves before content.
rationale: Over-tinted neutrals become extra accent colors.

title: Do not force brand hue into every component
rule: Use strong brand colors where they create recognition or hierarchy rather than as universal fill.
rationale: Overuse weakens both brand signal and component semantics.

title: Derive from dominant imagery when useful
rule: If a hero image or model dominates, sample or conceptually derive nearby neutrals and accents from it.
rationale: This helps DOM and media feel art-directed as one world.

title: Image-derived does not mean exact sampling
rule: Adjust sampled hues for contrast, hierarchy and screen use instead of blindly copying pixel colors.
rationale: Photography colors often need normalization for UI.

title: Separate decorative and functional colors
rule: Mark colors that are decorative-only versus colors safe for text, controls or status.
rationale: A beautiful swatch may be unusable for readable text.

title: Store safe text-on-accent pair
rule: Every primary accent should declare whether black, white or another foreground is the readable text color.
rationale: CTA readability should not be guessed per component.

title: Validate muted text explicitly
rule: Muted text must be tested on every surface where it appears.
rationale: Lower visual priority is not permission for unreadability.

title: Validate non-text UI contrast
rule: Borders, controls and focus indicators need sufficient contrast where accessibility rules require it.
rationale: Interfaces communicate through more than text.

title: Never use color alone for critical state
rule: Add iconography, label, shape or other cues for success, warning, error and selection when meaning matters.
rationale: Users may not perceive hue differences reliably.

title: Focus color is a core token
rule: Define focus-ring treatment at palette design time.
rationale: Keyboard interaction should not be patched after styling.

title: Do not create light mode by inversion
rule: Recompose surfaces, borders, accent intensity and imagery for light mode rather than mathematically inverting dark colors.
rationale: Optical balance differs between modes.

title: Do not create dark mode by blackening everything
rule: Use intentional luminance layers and adjust accent chroma for dark surroundings.
rationale: Dark themes need structure, not an empty black field.

title: Dark accent may need lower chroma
rule: An accent that works on white may become painfully intense on near-black.
rationale: Perceived intensity depends on context.

title: Light accent may need greater depth
rule: Very light accents may disappear on off-white surfaces.
rationale: Light themes often need darker accent tones for controls and text.

title: Pair warm near-black with warm off-white carefully
rule: Warm dark/light themes should share temperature without making every surface beige or brown.
rationale: Temperature coherence is useful; monotony is not.

title: Use OKLCH for controlled ramps when practical
rule: For generated systems, use perceptual lightness/chroma controls when browser/tooling constraints allow.
rationale: More predictable ramps make programmatic palettes easier to reason about.

title: Do not equate OKLCH values with accessibility
rule: Always run actual contrast checks after generating colors.
rationale: Perceptual uniformity and WCAG contrast are different concerns.

title: Generate hover states from role logic
rule: Derive hover/active states through controlled lightness/chroma shifts or structural feedback.
rationale: Random hex changes create inconsistent interaction.

title: Hover should not disappear in dark mode
rule: Check that interaction deltas remain visible on dark surfaces.
rationale: Small color changes can vanish at low luminance.

title: Selection requires persistent difference
rule: Selected state should remain visually distinct after hover ends.
rationale: Interaction state and hover state solve different problems.

title: 3D environment affects perceived material color
rule: Judge reflective materials with their environment and lights enabled.
rationale: Metal/glass appearance is inseparable from lighting context.

title: Coordinate DOM accent with scene accent
rule: Use related accent families across UI and WebGL unless deliberate contrast is part of the concept.
rationale: Independent palettes make the model look pasted behind the page.

title: Keep emissive color scarce
rule: Reserve emissive materials and bloom-driving colors for high-value details.
rationale: Too much emission destroys depth and hierarchy.

title: Use light temperature as narrative state
rule: Lighting temperature can shift across chapters if DOM tokens transition with it.
rationale: Synchronized changes create coherent scene storytelling.

title: Do not use cyan-magenta by default in 3D
rule: Choose 3D light colors from the project palette rather than the generic cyberpunk preset.
rationale: Creative-web clichés can be as repetitive as SaaS clichés.

title: Material albedo is not final perceived color
rule: Account for roughness, metalness, environment, tone mapping and post-processing.
rationale: Rendered color is contextual.

title: Tone mapping belongs in palette QA
rule: Evaluate the final render after tone mapping and post effects before locking DOM accents.
rationale: Rendering transforms can shift perceived values.

title: Bloom changes area perception
rule: A glowing accent visually occupies more area than its geometry.
rationale: Area guidance should include halo/bloom footprint.

title: Gradient endpoints need a relationship
rule: Choose gradient endpoints through material, harmony or narrative logic.
rationale: Two fashionable colors are not automatically a coherent gradient.

title: Gradient direction should support composition
rule: Align gradient direction with depth, lighting, movement or layout.
rationale: Arbitrary diagonal gradients often feel decorative and generic.

title: Use fewer gradient stops by default
rule: Begin with two meaningful endpoints and add stops only when needed.
rationale: Excess stops often introduce muddy intermediate colors.

title: Gradient text is a special effect
rule: Use gradient typography only when the text itself is a signature visual object.
rationale: Using it on every marketing headline destroys typographic clarity.

title: Status colors should remain semantically stable
rule: Success/warning/danger families should not change meaning across pages.
rationale: Semantic consistency matters more than section-level aesthetics.

title: Data colors need separability
rule: Categorical colors should be distinguishable in context and not merely aesthetically harmonious.
rationale: Data communication has different requirements from decorative branding.

title: Sequential data needs ordered lightness
rule: Use an ordered perceptual progression for low→high values.
rationale: Users should see magnitude order without memorizing labels.

title: Diverging data needs a meaningful midpoint
rule: Use two directional families only when the middle value is semantically meaningful.
rationale: Diverging color without a real midpoint can mislead.

title: Do not use brand accent for every chart series
rule: Create data-specific scales when multiple categories must be compared.
rationale: Brand color alone is not a data visualization system.

title: Palette names should describe intent
rule: Catalog recipes by mood/use/harmony/mode instead of vague names like cool-1.
rationale: Descriptive metadata improves agent retrieval.

title: Store harmony metadata
rule: Every catalog palette should declare monochromatic/analogous/complementary/etc.
rationale: Agents can then learn and retrieve by relationship rather than hex similarity.

title: Store role metadata
rule: Machine-readable recipes should label every swatch by UI role.
rationale: Roles make palettes composable.

title: Store contrast measurements
rule: Record verified contrast ratios for primary text pairs in recipe data.
rationale: This prevents agents from assuming readability.

title: Store area guidance
rule: Recipe metadata should suggest dominant/support/accent usage.
rationale: Area relationships are central to whether a palette works.

title: Store 3D notes
rule: Palettes intended for immersive sites should declare lighting/material guidance.
rationale: The same hex values behave differently in DOM and rendered scenes.

title: Store avoid-with metadata
rule: Document combinations that usually conflict, such as high-chroma dual accents plus heavy bloom.
rationale: Compatibility guidance reduces effect stacking.

title: Explain palette confidence
rule: Mark whether a recipe is source-observed, verified standard-based or synthesized.
rationale: Research integrity prevents false attribution.

title: Do not attribute generated recipes to creators
rule: Creator examples may inspire rules, but synthesized palettes must remain clearly labeled.
rationale: Avoid fabricated claims about what a designer recommends.

title: Use references as evidence, not authority
rule: A palette from an award-winning site still has to fit the new project.
rationale: Context-specific choices should not become universal laws.

title: Critique equal swatch previews
rule: Always preview a palette on a realistic UI composition in addition to equal color chips.
rationale: Screen-area relationships can reverse the impression of a swatch set.

title: Test grayscale hierarchy
rule: Temporarily remove chroma to see whether hierarchy survives on lightness/structure.
rationale: If the layout collapses without hue, colors may be doing too much structural work.

title: Test accent removal
rule: Remove the accent temporarily; content hierarchy should still mostly work.
rationale: Accent should enhance hierarchy rather than rescue a weak layout.

title: Test reduced color modes
rule: Consider forced-colors/high-contrast environments for functional content.
rationale: Robust interfaces should not depend on exact authored colors.

title: Teach with counterexamples
rule: When explaining a combination, mention one plausible misuse and why it fails.
rationale: Contrastive examples build reusable design judgment.

title: Offer alternatives by mood, not random colors
rule: If presenting multiple palettes, vary strategic direction such as restrained/energetic/editorial instead of random hue swaps.
rationale: Options should represent real art-direction choices.
